turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt900_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (O, Sb, Co, Si, Sn, Ca, Ni, Ti, Pb, Se, Ge, Cu, Zr, Te, S, Zn,
    Fe, Yb, Mn, Sr, Nb, Bi, Cd, Hf, In) and `target` (the measured zT
    (thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K).
  - b3_te_zt900_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 900 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".


The data files for this task are in your current working directory:
  - b3_te_zt900_train.csv
  - b3_te_zt900_pool.csv
Read them from disk. Give your answer as your final message — do not write it to a file.
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis

**Structure of the data.** Compositions are element fractions summing to ~1, so rows cluster into distinct material families. Element correlations with zT: Pb (+0.56), Te (+0.49), Se (+0.39), Hf (+0.23) positive; O (−0.47) strongly negative — all oxide-based entries have very low zT at 900 K.

**Top-performing training families:**
| Family | Best zT observed |
|---|---|
| Pb–Te(–S/Se/Sr) chalcogenides | 2.26, 2.21, 2.08, 2.03 |
| Cu₂Se (Cu≈0.65, Se≈0.33) | 1.74, 1.45, 1.17 |
| Half-Heusler Ni–Sn–Zr/Hf (Zr:Hf ≈ 0.13:0.20) | 1.35, 1.32, 1.21 |
| Skutterudite Co–Sb/Zr with Bi substitution | 1.33, 1.09 |

**Models.** 5-fold CV (log1p target): RF R²≈0.70, ET≈0.69, GB≈0.68. Ensembled 15 models (RF/ET/GB × 5 seeds) fitted on all 300 rows, cross-checked against a distance-weighted nearest-neighbour estimate in composition space (which also flags how well-supported each candidate is).

**Pool candidates ranking (ensemble pred / wkNN / nearest-train-distance):**
- **c052** — Pb 0.493, Te 0.394, S 0.099 → 1.52 / 1.49; nearest train neighbour (d=0.10) has zT = 2.21. Clearly the strongest.
- **c054** (Cu 0.651, Se 0.326) and **c063** (Cu 0.664, Se 0.336) → 1.43 / 1.18; sit essentially on top of the Cu₂Se points measured at 1.74, 1.45, 1.17.
- **c078** (Ni 0.333, Sn 0.330, Hf 0.200, Zr 0.133, Sb 0.003) → nearly identical to the best half-Heuslers measured at 1.21–1.35 (d = 0.003–0.012); very high-confidence ~1.2.
- **c057 / c086** (Co 0.333, Zr 0.333, Bi 0.25–0.27, Sn 0.067) → Bi-substituted skutterudites; the analogous train points give 1.09 and 1.33.
- Rejected: c025/c097 (bare Te 0.5, incomplete composition, far from any training point, d≈0.82 — unreliable extrapolation), c001/c006/c041 (plain PbTe with trace Bi: those exact analogues measured only 0.68–0.89), all O-containing rows (near-zero zT).

Between c057 and c086 I keep c057 (slight Sb co-substitution matches the 1.33 sample); c086 is the runner-up.

**Final: c052, c054, c063, c078, c057**

d=pd.read_csv('b3_te_zt900_train.csv'); p=pd.read_csv('b3_te_zt900_pool.csv')
cols=[c for c in d.columns if c!='target']
# family: for each pool row, mean target of 5 nearest train
X=d[cols].values;y=d.target.values
res=[]
for i,r in p.iterrows():
    dist=np.abs(X-r[cols].values.astype(float)).sum(1)
    o=np.argsort(dist)[:5]
    w=1/(dist[o]+0.05)
    res.append((r.candidate_id, (y[o]*w).sum()/w.sum(), y[o].max(), dist[o].mean()))
r=pd.DataFrame(res,columns=['id','wknn','nmax','dm']).sort_values('wknn',ascending=False)
print(r.head(12).round(3).to_string())
"
